verdict.rationale: Homebrew's own `brew tap` command adds custom repositories, and its two-argument form accepts any Git URL, so a platform engineer can point it at a self-hosted or internal tap. Taps can also ship their own bottles. Nothing in the evidence documents configurable mirrors or any scoped authentication mechanism, and a community report notes taps must be served over the git protocol rather than a static CDN-backed host. missing for 10: documented authentication/credential scoping for private taps or bottle hosts, configurable mirror endpoints for core/bottles/API, independent hands-on corroboration of private-registry setups.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can point the manager at private registries or mirrors with scoped authentication

citations.quote: The `brew tap` command adds repositories that Homebrew can use for formulae, casks and external commands.
the two-argument form accepts any URL supported by Git.
This may be useful for taps that wish to provide bottles for their formulae
